chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, from Sulayman ibn Khalid who said:
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: 'And to your Lord is the End (finality).' So if your speech reaches to Allah, then remain silent.

key_terms.الْمُنْتَهَى: The End / The Finality / The Limit

ai.seo_question: What does it mean when speech reaches to Allah according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Imam Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) utilizes the verse 'And to your Lord is the End' to establish the principle of *hadr* (restraint) in *kalam* (theology), advising believers to cease speculation when human intellect reaches its limit before the Divine. This hadith serves as a foundational text in Shia usul al-fiqh and kalam, warning against *ta'til* (denial of attributes) or *tashbih* (anthropomorphism) that arises from overextending reason beyond its valid scope.
